answer: Sybil resistance requires each identity to finish a Wesolowski-verifiable sequence of modular squarings, with every result depending on the previous one. GPUs can compute separate chains for separate clones, but cannot divide a single chain’s dependent steps to reduce its elapsed time; each added identity therefore needs parallel resources and still faces a sequential time floor. The proof verifies the work, not a shortcut: a ripple of checks can reveal hollow claims beneath a velvet interface.
